newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: OAU says seven African armies volunteer for Zaire.
newsitem.headline: OAU says seven African armies volunteer for Zaire.

text.p: Seven African countries are willing to commit troops to a multinational force for Zaire, the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) said on Wednesday.
OAU Secretary-General Salim Ahmed Salim said South Africa, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Congo, Cameroon, Senegal and Mali were the volunteers so far.
"This is not the end. Consultations for more troops contribution from African states are still going on," Salim told a news conference.
African leaders called last week for deployment of a "neutral force" to help 1.2 million Hutu refugees in eastern Zaire, displaced by a rebellion.

But there were protests in Africa when the U.N. Security Council said governments should pay for their own contingents. African leaders say their states are too poor to pay and should be financed by others.
"Africa expects that the fund for the neutral force should be channeled through the United Nations," Salim said.
"It is very important that the assistance to be provided should be global. We do not believe...that the assistance should be on a bilateral basis," he said.
He welcomed Canada's offer to lead the multinational force.

"Canada has a long history in peacekeeping in the world. It is an exemplary country in terms of peacekeeping -- a country of long experience and highly respected by African countries in general," he said.
Salim said it was early to talk about where the force should be based -- a central and still unresolved issue.
"In any event, I am not a military man. This decision would be better left to those who lead the troops," he said.
